column1: # The divergence.broiler-js and divergence.broiler-vm fields corpus revision 9 retires: every numerics
# vector Broiler.JS matches after milestone SJL-4.5's cut-over (Broiler.JS/CHANGELOG.md lists the
# corrections) and every one Broiler.VM matches after milestone SJL-4.4's (its JSD-0069 lists them), under
# the reason scripts/conformance/numerics-divergences.txt gave it at revision 8. The reasons' text follows

# js-asuintn-wide: BigInt.asUintN converts a width of 2^32 or more to a 32-bit integer, so the modulus is wrong, giving a wrong value, or zero, raising a .NET DivideByZeroException, where the result of a negative value is past any representation and a RangeError. Answered by Broiler.JS docs/roadmap/SharedLibraries.md, SJL-4.5 (the correction of asUintN at very large widths).

# js-bigint-hex-parse: StringToBigInt does not complete within the runner's limit for a hexadecimal text of 262,144 digits, because each digit multiplies the whole value. Answered by Broiler.JS docs/roadmap/SharedLibraries.md, SJL-4.5 (the BigInt kernel's parse replaces TryParsePrefixedDigits).

# js-bigint-key: A BigInt property key beyond 2^32 - 1 or below 0 raises a .NET OverflowException that escapes the engine, where the key is the BigInt's decimal text. Answered by Broiler.JS docs/roadmap/SharedLibraries.md, SJL-4.5 (the correction of BigInt property keys beyond 2^32 - 1 and below 0).

# js-bigint-power-exponent: BigInt exponentiation converts the exponent to a 32-bit integer, so an exponent of 2^31 or more raises a .NET OverflowException that escapes the engine, where 1n, -1n and 0n have their exact powers and any other base is a RangeError at the representation's limit. Answered by Broiler.JS docs/roadmap/SharedLibraries.md, SJL-4.5 (the BigInt kernel; the correction of Power's 32-bit exponent).

# js-cbrt-rounding: Math.cbrt is not correctly rounded: it chooses among neighbours of the platform's root by a test in double arithmetic, and can be a unit in the last place away, an exact cube root included. Answered by Broiler.JS docs/roadmap/SharedLibraries.md, SJL-4.5 (JSMath's cbrt moves to the library, JSD-0067 decision 5).

# js-expm1-log1p: Math.expm1 and Math.log1p are more than a unit in the last place from the exact value on some inputs: the Kahan-style correction gives -1.00075 for Math.expm1(-745) and an infinity just below expm1's overflow threshold. Answered by Broiler.JS docs/roadmap/SharedLibraries.md, SJL-4.5 (JSMath's expm1 and log1p move to the library, JSD-0067 decision 5).

# js-hypot-pairwise: Math.hypot of three or more arguments is computed pairwise, rounding at each step, and is more than a unit in the last place from the exact value on some inputs, a hypotenuse that is itself a double included (Math.hypot(2, 10, 11) is not 15). Answered by Broiler.JS docs/roadmap/SharedLibraries.md, SJL-4.5 (JSMath's hypot moves to the library, JSD-0067 decision 5).

# js-pow-one-nan: 1 ** NaN gives 1 on the generic and the numeric paths, and 1 ** Infinity and 1 ** -Infinity written as literals give 1, where each is NaN: the generic JSValue.Power lacks the NaN-exponent case and the compiled paths emit Math.Pow. Math.pow gives NaN. Answered by Broiler.JS docs/roadmap/SharedLibraries.md, SJL-4.5 (the correction of 1 ** NaN on every path and the cases of 1 to an infinity on the compiled paths).

# vm-cbrt-rounding: Math.cbrt snaps the platform's root only when it cubes back exactly, so it is not correctly rounded: it can be a unit in the last place away, an exact cube root included (Math.cbrt(0.125) is 0.49999999999999994). Answered by Broiler.VM docs/javascript-shared-libraries/milestones/sjl-4-numerics.md, SJL-4.4 (JSD-0067 decision 5).

# vm-expm1-log1p: Math.expm1 and Math.log1p compute exp(x) - 1 and log(x + 1), which is what double.ExpM1 and double.LogP1 do on .NET 10, so they lose their significant digits near zero: below 2^-53 the result is 0, and elsewhere it can be far more than a unit in the last place from the exact value. Answered by Broiler.VM docs/javascript-shared-libraries/milestones/sjl-4-numerics.md, SJL-4.4 (JSD-0067 decision 5).

# vm-hypot-rounding: Math.hypot scales by the largest argument in one pass and is more than a unit in the last place from the exact value on some inputs, a hypotenuse that is itself a double included (Math.hypot(2, 10, 11) is not 15). Answered by Broiler.VM docs/javascript-shared-libraries/milestones/sjl-4-numerics.md, SJL-4.4 (JSD-0067 decision 5).

# vm-sum-precise-flush: Math.sumPrecise scales its terms when the largest is huge, which flushes a tiny term to zero: Math.sumPrecise([1e308, -1e308, 5e-324]) is 0. Answered by Broiler.VM docs/javascript-shared-libraries/milestones/sjl-4-numerics.md, SJL-4.4 (the PreciseSum accumulator, JSD-0067 decision 5).
